stages.description: Input fuse, reverse-polarity diode, input cap
stages.fail_note: No input voltage. Check the input fuse, reverse-polarity diode, and the input source.
Input present at connector but wrong at the regulator input pin. Check the input trace and decoupling.

stages.description: Controller VCC (internal LDO or external bias)
stages.fail_note: Controller VCC missing. The IC cannot run. Check the VCC decoupling cap and the VCC feed (internal LDO or bias winding).
Controller not enabled or no reference. Check EN source and the internal Vref.

stages.description: Switch (N-MOSFET) to ground; charging the inductor
stages.fail_note: No switching. The boost switch must toggle to charge the inductor. Dead gate-drive = controller fault.
Inductor fault. An open inductor breaks the boost path.

stages.description: Output boost diode (schottky) — blocks reverse current
stages.fail_note: Boost diode fault. An OPEN boost diode means the output cannot rise (no charge path to the output cap). A SHORT boost diode drains the output back to the switch. This is structurally distinct from a buck's rectifier.

stages.description: Output cap (charged through the boost diode)
Non-isolated feedback: output divider to controller FB pin
stages.fail_note: Feedback pin not at expected voltage. Check the FB divider resistors and FB decoupling cap.
PGOOD not asserted or protection tripping. Check the PGOOD pull-up and the OVP/OCP monitors.

fault_patterns.notes: Boost: an open boost diode is a common no-output cause.
Boost overvoltage = shorted switch or open FB.
Output present but wrong voltage. Check the feedback divider and the reference.
Output unstable/oscillating. Check output caps, feedback compensation, ESR.
